tip: The main footage of a video, usually the people talking.
meaning: A-roll is the main story: the interview, the host, the action. The extra pictures that cover it are B-roll.
example: A person telling their story on camera.

tip: Extra footage that covers or illustrates the main story.
meaning: While someone talks about their bakery, you show the oven, the dough and the shop sign. Those pictures are B-roll. They add interest and hide cuts.
example: Hands kneading dough while the baker's voice is heard.

tip: A first, untidy version that has the right pieces in the right order.
meaning: In a rough cut the story is there, but the timing, sound and colour are not finished.
example: A first assembly of all the best moments of the trip, in order.

tip: A nearly finished version where timing is polished.
meaning: The fine cut has tidy cuts and pace. Only small changes and finishing touches remain.
example: The version you show to the teacher for the last comments.

tip: The moment when the picture edit is final and cannot change anymore.
meaning: After picture lock, the sound, music and colour teams do their work on a fixed timeline. A change to the picture would break their work.
example: "We have picture lock, send it to the sound mix."

tip: All the work after filming: editing, sound, colour and effects.
meaning: Post (for short) is the part of making a video that happens once the shooting is done.
example: After filming the trip, you spend a week in post.

tip: The planning before filming: script, storyboard, locations and schedule.
meaning: Pre-production is everything you decide before the camera rolls, so the shooting is fast and calm.
example: Writing what you will say and choosing where to film.

tip: The time when the footage is filmed.
meaning: Production is the shooting: cameras, actors, sound, lights.
example: The weekend you film the whole short movie.

tip: A joke about leaving a problem to the editor instead of fixing it on set.
meaning: Sometimes small problems can be repaired when editing, but it is always better to get it right when filming.
example: A boom microphone appears in a corner; "we will fix it in post".

tip: What people say when filming is finished.
meaning: "Wrap" means the shooting of a scene, a day or the whole film is done.
example: "That's a wrap, thank you everybody!"

tip: A series of drawings that plan the shots before filming.
meaning: A storyboard looks like a comic strip: one box for each shot, with a note about what happens.
example: A sketch of a close-up of the cake, then a wide of the party.

tip: A checklist of all the shots you need to film.
meaning: A shot list lists each shot, so you do not forget one before leaving the place.
example: "Wide of the door, close-up of the hand, cutaway of the clock."

tip: The written plan of what is said and what happens.
meaning: A script has the words people say and a description of what we see. Even a 30-second video can have one.
example: Three lines of narration for a product video.

tip: Filming a scene from several angles so the editor has choices.
meaning: Good coverage means a wide shot, a medium and some close-ups of the same action. The editor can then choose the best moments and keep the pace.
example: Filming the same conversation from both sides.

tip: A wide shot of a whole scene from beginning to end.
meaning: The master shot shows everything that happens. Other angles are cut into it.
example: A wide shot of a whole dinner table scene.

tip: A shot filmed later to fill a gap or fix a missing piece.
meaning: Sometimes the editor notices something is missing. A pickup shot is a small extra shot made afterwards.
example: A close-up of the key in the lock, filmed a week later.

tip: The best-looking shot of the main subject.
meaning: A hero shot shows the product or the person at their best, the shot you would put on a poster.
example: The sneaker shining on a pedestal.

tip: Starting a video directly with action, before the title.
meaning: A cold open puts you in the middle of something exciting, and the opening titles come after.
example: A funny moment first, then the show's title.

tip: A fast, exciting video that shows the best bits to sell an idea.
meaning: A sizzle reel is a pitch video: it shows the most attractive moments in a very short time.
example: A one-minute highlight of a band to convince a venue to book it.

tip: A short video of someone's best work, used like a portfolio.
meaning: Editors, actors and designers make showreels to show what they can do.
example: A one-minute compilation of your best edits.

tip: The person who decides how the story is told.
meaning: The director leads the team, chooses how each shot looks and works with actors.
example: The person who says "Action!" and "Cut!".

tip: The person who organises the money, the people and the schedule.
meaning: A producer makes it possible for the film to happen: finds money, hires people, solves problems.
example: The person who books the location and pays for the equipment.

tip: The person in charge of how the picture looks: light and camera.
meaning: The DP (or cinematographer) chooses the camera, the lenses and the lighting to create the look.
example: The person who makes the sunset scene look golden.

tip: The chief of lighting on a film crew.
meaning: The gaffer plans and sets up the lights, working with the director of photography.
example: The person who places a big lamp to make moonlight.

tip: A crew member who moves and holds the camera gear and the supports.
meaning: Grips build rigs, dolly tracks and stands for lights and cameras.
example: The people who push the camera on rails.

tip: The person who holds the microphone on a long pole over the actors.
meaning: The boom operator keeps the microphone close to people but out of the picture.
example: Someone holding a furry microphone just above the actors' heads.

tip: An entry-level crew member who helps wherever needed.
meaning: A runner (or production assistant) fetches things, carries equipment and passes messages. Many careers start here.
example: The person who brings coffee and sets up chairs.

tip: A page that tells the crew where to be and when.
meaning: A call sheet lists the time, the place, the scenes and who is needed for a filming day.
example: "Be at the park at 7:00 for scenes 4 and 5."

tip: The footage from the last filming day, watched the next day.
meaning: Dailies (or rushes) let the director and editors check what was filmed, so mistakes are caught early.
example: Everyone watches yesterday's clips at lunch.

tip: Planning where people stand and move, and where the camera goes.
meaning: Blocking is working out the movements of actors and camera for a scene, before filming it.
example: Marking on the floor with tape where each actor stops.

tip: Where deleted footage goes, as a saying.
meaning: "It ended up on the cutting room floor" means it was filmed but not used in the final video.
example: A funny scene removed because the video was too long.

tip: A writer's rule: cut what you love if it does not help the story.
meaning: Editors use it too: a beautiful shot that slows down the story has to go.
example: Removing your favourite shot because the video is better without it.

tip: Text added to the picture, like names and news tickers.
meaning: "Chyron" is the name TV people use for graphics such as names and headlines.
example: The scrolling headline at the bottom of a news channel.

tip: A short clip between parts of a show, usually with a logo.
meaning: A bumper is a few seconds that marks the break between segments.
example: A two-second logo animation before the ads.

tip: Zooming into the picture a bit, to make a shot feel closer.
meaning: A punch-in enlarges part of the frame, so the same shot gets a new feel and can be used as a second angle.
example: Zooming 120% on the speaker's face for emphasis.

tip: Making a cut, a move or a text arrive exactly on a beat of the music.
meaning: When something "hits" the beat, it lands at the same moment as the drum. It makes a video feel tight.
example: Each title appears exactly when the snare plays.

tip: A shot or a scene that has been filmed and is done.
meaning: The old film was kept in cans. "In the can" means the scene is recorded and safe.
example: "That scene is in the can."

tip: A collection of pictures that show the style you want.
meaning: A mood board gathers colours, photos and examples to tell a team what feeling the video should have.
example: A board with photos of golden sunsets for a warm summer video.
